cases.question: Why can MODIS and VIIRS sensors report different counts? Cite NASA documentation.
cases.answer:
Source-based notes (curated paraphrases):

VIIRS 375 m data complements MODIS detections. Its improved resolution responds better to relatively small fires and maps large fire perimeters in more detail, so MODIS and VIIRS counts can differ.

MODIS records locate the center of a 1 km hotspot pixel, not necessarily an individual fire. One pixel can contain multiple fires. Satellite hotspot detections are not a count of distinct fires.

Evidence: [VIIRS spatial resolution](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/content/descriptions/FIRMS_VIIRS_Firehotspots.html); [MODIS pixel definition](https://firms2.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/descriptions/FIRMS_MODIS_Firehotspots.html)

Supported scope: 37–42°N, 125–119°W; complete UTC weeks in 2023–2025.
